items.t: Will oppose tax increases and work to reduce government spending.
items.q: He will oppose tax increases and fight to reduce wasteful government spending so that Mainers can keep more of what they earn.

items.t: Wants property tax relief and is against expanding the income tax.
items.q: As a State Senator, he will champion property tax relief, oppose efforts to expand the income tax, and push for a state budget that prioritizes essential services without growing government bureaucracy.

items.t: Wants to cut red tape and reduce regulatory costs for small businesses.
items.q: He will work to cut red tape, reduce regulatory costs, and ensure that Maine is open for business.

items.t: Has consistently voted against budget proposals in the legislature.
items.q: Billy Bob has been a consistent vote against budget-busting proposals in the legislature and has pushed for greater transparency and accountability in how taxpayer dollars are spent.

items.t: Supports strong law enforcement, is against sanctuary city policies, and wants Maine to take a firm stand on border security and illegal immigration.
items.q: He supports strong law enforcement, opposes sanctuary city policies, and will push for Maine to take a firm stand on border security and illegal immigration.

items.t: Supports Maine's Constitutional Carry law and is against red flag laws and magazine bans.
items.q: He supports Maine's Constitutional Carry law and will stand firmly against any attempt to impose red flag laws, magazine bans, or other restrictions that erode the constitutional rights of Mainers.

items.t: Has voted against gun control measures.
items.q: He has consistently voted against gun control measures that would punish law-abiding citizens while doing nothing to address the root causes of crime.

items.t: Will oppose energy development that he says threatens productive fishing grounds.
items.q: In the Senate, he will work to ensure Maine has a strong voice in federal fisheries management, oppose energy development that threatens productive fishing grounds, and cut unnecessary state-level red tape

items.t: Wants to protect people's ability to grow gardens and to grow and raise their own food.
items.q: We want to protect people’s ability to grow gardens, grow and raise their own food.

items.t: Said the food amendment is a response to growing corporate ownership of the food supply.
items.q: Faulkingham and others said the amendment is a response to growing corporate ownership of the food supply.

items.t: Said local rules would still be enforced under the food amendment.
items.q: Supporters of the proposal, including Faulkingham, said that local rules would still be enforced, and that the amendment would not mean you could do things like raise chickens anywhere you want

items.t: Will push back against federal and state regulations affecting fishermen.
items.q: He will fight to push back against overreaching federal and state regulations that are driving fishermen out of business.

items.t: Is against eminent domain abuse and overreaching land use regulations.
items.q: He will stand against eminent domain abuse, overreaching land use regulations, and any effort to limit how Maine families can use their land.

record.t: Requested a division on the vote on Passage to be Enacted, and the bill passed the House 79 to 67.

record.t: Proposed a constitutional amendment that he likened to a "2nd Amendment of food".
record.q: The proposal is essentially “the 2nd Amendment of food,” said Republican Rep. Billy Bob Faulkingham, who proposed the amendment, likening it to the U.S. constitutional amendment that assures the right to bear arms.
